title: From soprano and tenor back to clarinet for good
summary: Retells that he took up the new soprano and tenor saxophones, then returned to clarinet when Oliver bought him one, and now never plays saxophone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: So then the soprano came out, the soprano saxophone, and I kind of liked that. And I got the tenor first but then I'd take the part of the clarinet because the music was written, like, another chorus would be for clarinet and one would, you

know, the sax. And I kind of liked that so I got that and I put the clarinet down and forgot all about it till I went to Chicago, and that's when Albert and Darnell left to go to China. I wouldn't go.

And King Oliver -- I told you about King Oliver buying me this clarinet. He asked me did I play it. I said, "Well, yes." He says, "Well, if I get you one, will you try?" I said, "Sure, I'll try. What have I got to lose?" And he got it and I started woodshedding, and I started to thinking, "Well, gee, I can play more than I ever did play," I mean, you know. And I kept going at it like that. Then I began to like that better than I did sax, and so I just kept at it, and that's the way it is. I don't play sax anymore.
You never played saxophone again after that?
No, I won't play it. I don't like it anymore. And so that's the way that happened.
